newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Srilanka calls for restraint by U.S. and Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Srilanka calls for restraint by U.S. and Iraq.

text.p: Sri Lanka, expressing concern over escalating tension in Iraq, called on Friday on both the United States and Iraq to exercise restraint.
"Sri Lanka is concerned that recent developments in the Republic of Iraq and the missile attacks on that country are escalating tensions in the region," a Foreign Ministry statment said.

"The government of Sri Lanka would urge the parties concerned to exercise restraint in order to alleviate suffering among the people of Iraq as well as to prevent deterioration of a situation which may pose a threat to regional and international peace and security," it said.

U.S. forces fired a total of 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday. The attacks were prompted by the Iraqi army's incursion into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq last Saturday.
"It is desirable that internal conflicts in the northern part of Iraq, which appear to have precipitated the current situation, be settled through negotiations," the statement said.
